source: CIE Mechanics 练习册(学生版),9 章，每章题目注明出处(9709_s17_qp_41 等,2016–2020)

1.name: Velocity and acceleration
1.scope: constant acceleration along a line: the suvat formulae, displacement-time and velocity-time graphs made of straight lines (gradient, area), vertical motion under gravity, two particles meeting or overtaking

2.name: Force and motion in one dimension
2.scope: Newton's second law for one body moving along a line: F = ma with weight, a driving force and a resistance, lifts and vertical motion with forces, no resolving at an angle and no friction coefficient

3.name: Forces in two dimensions
3.scope: resolving forces at angles: resultant of several forces, equilibrium of a particle under three or more forces, a particle on a smooth inclined plane, forces on a particle held by strings

4.name: Friction
4.scope: the model F ≤ μR: limiting friction, coefficient of friction, a particle on a rough horizontal or inclined plane, about to slip or moving with friction

5.name: Connected particles
5.scope: two or more bodies joined by strings, rods or couplings: pulleys and pegs, a particle on a table or plane connected over a pulley to a hanging particle, car and trailer or tow bar, tension and thrust, motion after the string breaks or a particle reaches the ground

6.name: General motion in a straight line
6.scope: variable acceleration: velocity or displacement given as a function of time, differentiating and integrating to find acceleration, velocity or distance, maximum velocity, times at rest, change of direction

7.name: Momentum
7.scope: conservation of momentum in collisions along a line: coalescing particles, change of direction, a series of collisions, loss of kinetic energy in a collision

8.name: Work and energy
8.scope: work done by a force (including at an angle), kinetic energy, gravitational potential energy, conservation of mechanical energy on smooth surfaces or slopes

9.name: The work-energy principle and power
9.scope: the work-energy principle with work done against resistance or friction, power P = Fv, driving force of a car or cyclist, maximum or steady speed, rate of working on a slope
